title: Armenia (301)
hook: a kingdom turns to Christ through Gregory the Illuminator, after years in a pit

segments.voice: Yesterday, Frumentius, the boy under the tree who came back a bishop. Your line was the church of the ark. What did you learn about Ethiopia? Day seven hundred ninety-six.

A man in the king's service is told to honor the king's goddess, and he says no. He's a Christian. So the king has him thrown into a deep pit under a royal fortress, and leaves him there in the dark. Up above, time goes by and people forget him. The king assumes he's long dead. But in the way the Armenian story is told, one person hasn't forgotten: a woman who comes to the edge and keeps him alive with food let down into the dark. Today, the man in the pit, and the kingdom that came looking for him.

The man's name is Gregory, and the story comes from the old Armenian history that goes under the name of Agathangelos. The king is Tiridates. While Gregory is in the pit, the king does worse things. A group of Christian women, fleeing, come to Armenia, and when one of them, Hripsime, refuses the king, he has them killed. Then, the history says, the king is struck down, his mind broken, living like a wild animal. His sister has a dream, more than once: only Gregory can heal him. Everyone is sure Gregory is dead. They go to the pit anyway, lower a rope, and call down. And a voice answers. They pull him out, thin and blackened, but alive. Gregory goes to the king, and the king is healed. Gregory gathers the bones of the women who were killed and buries them with honor. He preaches, and the king who threw him in the pit is baptized. In the Armenian telling, this is the moment the kingdom turned to Christ. Tradition points to the place, and pilgrims still go there: Khor Virap, the deep pit. And Armenians gave Gregory a name: the Illuminator, the one who brought light. There's a line in the Psalms that fits him almost too well, in the old King James words: "He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock." Light came up out of a hole in the ground.

Here's the practice: hold Armenia in mind. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the people of Armenia, and Armenians living far from it, wherever they are, carrying their own church and their own alphabet with them. You don't need to know much. Just picture a family at a table, a church on a hill, a grandmother lighting a candle. Then let your mind rest on anyone you know who is in a pit right now, the kind no one else sees. If you pray, you can pray for Armenia, and for them. If you don't, just hold them in the light for this sit. The bell holds the time.
Armenia. The kingdom whose story turns on a man in a pit, pulled out alive, who became Gregory the Illuminator.
Your line: light from a pit. Today, get something good to someone in a hard place: a message, a meal, a call. Day seven hundred ninety-six.

howItsDone: The Armenian Apostolic Church traces its roots to the apostles Thaddeus and Bartholomew and honors Saint Gregory the Illuminator as the one who brought the faith to the kingdom and as its first chief bishop; Armenian Catholics honor him too, and pilgrims visit the monastery at Khor Virap, built over the pit where tradition says he was held.

original.note: Armenian: the deep pit, the name of the place where tradition says Gregory was held.

trapdoor: what you thought: Armenia became Christian when its king decided to.
what it means: a king who threw a Christian in a pit was healed by him, and the kingdom turned to Christ.
what a scholar hears: Agathangelos's history, Hripsime's martyrdom, and Gregory's title, Lusavorich, the Illuminator.

notes: The index title keeps '(301)' (kept exactly, as required) but the script states no date; the traditional date (301, sometimes 314) is not in the cited text. The index hook said 'the first kingdom to become Christian'; the script attributes 'first Christian nation' to Armenian Christians. Confirm.

Agathangelos: Gregory refuses to honor Anahit; the pit at Artashat; the years (traditionally thirteen or fifteen) are left out; the woman lowering bread is told as how the story goes; Hripsime and companions martyred; Tiridates' madness (told as being turned boar-like); his sister Khosrovidukht's repeated dream; Gregory drawn out alive; healing; baptism. Paraphrased; confirm each.
Khor Virap (Խոր Վիրապ, 'deep pit') and Lusavorich ('Illuminator'): confirm spelling and pronunciation.

Practice reworded from the index ('pray for Armenia') to an invitation: 'if you pray, you can pray for Armenia'. It mentions the Armenian alphabet and diaspora without dates; confirm. No reference to modern politics or the 1915 genocide, deliberately.
howItsDone: Armenian Catholic veneration and the Khor Virap monastery: confirm.
